messages:
maria: Hey team — noticed a docs PR (https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/458) where the reroute header example is inconsistent between the cURL and Python snippets. cURL uses "X-Redwood-Route" but the Python snippet sets "x-redwood-route" in headers. We should standardize casing and also clarify whether the header is required or optional.

kevin: thanks for flagging. which endpoint is this for?

maria: GET /v1/generate — example in api-ref/generate.md. The cURL example also has a small typo in the header value: "canary" vs "canary-region" in the python snippet.

kevin: ah ok. cc @sam since SDK examples are affected. sam: can you confirm runtime accepts either case?

sam: runtime normalizes headers but we prefer canonical Pascal-case style for docs: X-Redwood-Route. It'll accept lowercase but callers shouldn't rely on that. Also the allowed values are: "default", "canary", "eu" — not "canary-region".

olivia: good to know. I'll update the wording to say "Optional header to prefer a routing pool; accepted values: default, canary, eu. Header name is X-Redwood-Route (case-insensitive)." Any objections?

maria: sounds good. Can we also fix the Python snippet to use requests properly? Current snippet uses:
```python
headers = {"x-redwood-route": "canary-region", "Authorization": f"Bearer {API_KEY}"}
resp = requests.post(url, json=payload, headers=headers)
```
We should change to:
```python
headers = {"X-Redwood-Route": "canary", "Authorization": f"Bearer {API_KEY}"}
resp = requests.post(url, json=payload, headers=headers)
```

sam: ACK. I'll push a quick PR to the SDK-snippets repo with the corrected python snippet and a test that the docs generator picks it up.

docs-bot: PR linked: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/458 — CI: failed (lint: excerpt-check).

kevin: lint failure is because we have a mismatch between the codeblock language hint and the snippet. It expects \`python\` but the file has none. Olivia can you add the language hint and update the example text?

olivia: will do. Also adding a short migration note: "Old examples used "canary-region"; use "canary" now." Anything else?

maria: add a tiny unit test in docs/tests/snippets_test.py that asserts header string appears in generated html. Then this CI lint will be happier.

sam: done — PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-snippets/pull/102 created, includes updated snippet and test.

docs-bot: docs PR CI now: passing (after fixes).

maria: great — final ask: can we add a one-line note in the api-ref generate.md showing server behavior when header missing (falls back to default routing and logs route-suggestion in trace). kevin can you confirm trace behavior?

kevin: confirmed — request will be routed to default and trace will include route_suggestion: null. I'll add the exact wording: "If X-Redwood-Route is omitted, requests are routed to the default pool; traces will contain route_suggestion: null."

olivia: PR updated with wording, snippet language hints, and migration note. Merging now. :shipit:

maria: thanks all!
